scope.name: Private Table Formation and Campaign Onboarding
in_scope: establish the durable Group human-continuity record and GroupMembership boundary without cloning Campaign/Session membership
private Group creation and invite-based joining for existing real-world groups
separate Group membership from Campaign participation, seats, roles and Character control
private interest/join-request workflow with sparse profiles and hard compatibility fields only where explicitly supplied
trial-table, guest, guest-pool and return/hiatus membership states
explicit seat policy, waitlist policy and transparent seat-offer rationale
GM/organizer pool, observer and co-GM onboarding through existing permission/role owners
campaign/one-shot/Game Event attachment to the Group and one-shot-to-persistent-Group continuity
campaign expectations preview sufficient for private onboarding without implementing Session Zero
invite-link and QR join handoff using existing invitation authority where technically applicable
deterministic private-table golden flow from Group creation through successful Campaign onboarding
out_of_scope: public LFG, public game discovery or stranger matchmaking
public profiles, ratings, reputation or human reliability scoring
real-world scheduling, RSVP, calendar integration or attendance tracking
Session Zero, Consent/Veils or table-agreement implementation
marketplace, paid GM commerce, subscriptions or creator monetization
community moderation beyond the private safety/permission controls already required by existing owners
GPR implementation changes outside explicit integration contracts

locked_principles: Multiversal treats the people as more durable than the game they are currently playing.
Group membership and Campaign participation are independent lifecycles.
Hard compatibility is explainable before any soft recommendation.
Accession is mutual where ongoing participation requires mutual participation.
No public generalized human reliability or desirability score.
Common private onboarding remains useful with sparse information.
